text:
Samira Khan: Quick sync — planning a staged publish for Python + TS SDKs during the 02:00 UTC change window. Goal: validate pin propagation behavior and include a short deprecation note for the legacy sync client. Need final signoff on publish steps, release notes blurb, and rollback criteria.
Noah Bell: I can run the publish and monitor. What are the artifact tags?
Samira Khan: Using `v2.3.1-rc1-canary` for canary. Artifacts: `redwood-sdk-python` wheel/sdist to testpypi, `@redwood/sdk-ts` to npm with `canary` tag. Release notes will include migration snippet for sync->async.
Noah Bell: OK. I'll follow the usual build/publish steps and attach logs here.
Samira Khan: deploy-bot, schedule the canary at 1746001400 and report back.
deploy-bot: scheduled job #deploy-912 at 1746001400 for packages: redwood-sdk-python, @redwood/sdk-ts. Canary tag: v2.3.1-rc1-canary. CI: https://ci.internal/jobs/deploy-912 :rocket:
Noah Bell: publishing steps I plan to run:
```bash
# build artifacts
make build-sdks
# python -> upload to testpypi
twine upload --repository testpypi dist/redwood_sdk_python-2.3.1rc1.whl
# ts -> npm canary tag
cd packages/sdk-ts && npm publish --tag canary
```
Clara Ruiz: I'll update the release notes and add a short migration snippet in docs. Will link the migration script in the blurb. PR inbound.
Dev Support Bot: FYI: Support runbook updated with provisional messaging for canary regressions. Ticket template: SUP-RED-178.
deploy-bot: job deploy-912 started at 1746001400. step: build -> success. step: publish TS -> success. python upload -> success to testpypi.
Clara Ruiz: kicking off smoke suite now: auth refresh, streaming, embed-size-check, install/pinning behavior. Running `./scripts/smoke/canary_checks.sh`.
Noah Bell: watching logs, updating tracking link: https://internal/tracking/releases/2.3.1-rc1
Clara Ruiz: smoke results: streaming ok, embeddings OK, install/pin behavior ok but token refresh shows sporadic 401 on refresh endpoint for two replicas.
Samira Khan: hold propagation. Noah, please remove canary routing and yank npm tag while we triage.
Noah Bell: removed console route `canary-v2.3.1` and ran `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary`.
deploy-bot: noted: route canary-v2.3.1 removed.
Clara Ruiz: logs indicate `invalid_claims` on refresh. Repro locally against that auth replica.
Noah Bell: rollback plan: 
- revoke canary dist-tags (`npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary`)
- remove testpypi artifact via admin UI and hold stable pypi publish
- disable canary routing in console
- notify support + post short customer notice in release notes under "Canary status"
Samira Khan: good. Can we get a quick mitigation to unblock customers if they hit the issue?
Clara Ruiz: mitigation: restart auth sidecar pod for affected cluster, that resets the cache for token keys. I'll add this to the notes.
Noah Bell: cutting rc1.1 after patch. ETA 30-45m once auth PR lands. Will republish with `v2.3.1-rc1.1` and re-run the same canary matrix.
Dev Support Bot: Notifying support team channel: "Canary rc1 had token-refresh regression; canary routing disabled. If customers see 401 refresh, restart auth sidecar or wait for patched SDK rc1.1."
Samira Khan: docs: include pin guidance: for canary show `pip install redwood-sdk-python==2.3.1rc1` and `npm install @redwood/sdk-ts@canary` and a warning about not using canary in prod. For GA we recommend exact pin `==2.3.1`.
Clara Ruiz: PR for docs and release notes: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/501 — includes migration snippet and a "Known issue" entry.
Noah Bell: once rc1.1 is out, we'll run an extended smoke run for 60 minutes before promoting. If no auth errors, proceed to GA shiproom. Rollback criteria: any reproducible token-refresh 4xx > 2 hosts OR streaming regressions > 5% error rate.
Samira Khan: thanks. Tracking ticket REL-229 created. We'll reconvene in this thread when rc1.1 is published. :white_check_mark:
